kanban-claude 0.2.0.dev9

The runner, not the agent file, now decides which built-in tools each dispatched role gets. The owner can make a list longer or shorter with one config command. This page explains what changed and why.

Release explainer, 2026-10-20. Diff v0.2.0.dev8 (7b78b15) to 2a4aee8 (feature/runner-tool-lists). Dev pre-release.

Background

What was in the agent files, and why it moved

kanban-claude starts one Claude Code run per card with claude -p --agent kanban-claude:<role>. Five roles are dispatched this way: smith, designer, scout, warden and the optional atlassian role. Until dev8, each role's agent file in plugins/kanban-claude/agents/ carried a tools: allowlist. It named the built-in tools, the one subagent type the role could start (Agent(kanban-claude:card-helper)), the MCP servers it could use, and, for atlassian, 17 exact mcp__atlassian__* tool names.

The owner wanted the orchestrator side, meaning the runner, to form that list, so it can be deliberately long or short for each role without touching an agent file. dev9 is that one change. It does not touch the board, the database schema or the review flow.

Three details of Claude Code shape the design. --tools takes built-in tool names and cannot name an Agent(type). Its list applies inside subagents too. And a PreToolUse hook that exits 2 blocks the call. The walkthrough shows how each is used. Line numbers are in plugins/kanban-claude/runtime/src/kanban_claude/ at 2a4aee8 unless a path says otherwise.

Change diagram

Which components changed, and how

  • + added
  • ~ changed
  • − removed
  • = left as it was

Arrows show how the pieces feed each other when a run starts. The runner reads the store, passes --agent and --tools to claude -p, writes the run's settings (with the hook) and its MCP file, and the tests check all of it. Every item is explained in the walkthrough.

Walkthrough

Area by area

Each area says what changed, why, and how you notice it as the operator.

The runner forms each role's tool list +added~changed−removed

What changed
store.py:194-204 adds five config keys, tools.smith, tools.designer, tools.scout, tools.warden and tools.atlassian, each a list of built-in tool names. build_argv (runner.py:295) takes the list as a new last argument and passes it as --tools (runner.py:305); the run reads it from tools.<role> at runner.py:463. config_set refuses a tools.* value with a non-string item (store.py:376). The agent files of the five dispatched roles now say tools: "*", so they no longer list anything; card-checker, card-helper and review-helper keep explicit lists. The defaults reproduce what the agent files listed, minus the mcp__ names and the Agent(…) grants (see below). Smith, designer, scout and warden default to a list that starts with Agent; atlassian gets Bash, Read, Skill, ToolSearch, ListMcpResourcesTool, ReadMcpResourceTool and no Agent.
Why
The owner wanted the runner to form the list, so it can be made deliberately long or short for a role without editing an agent file. Per-card lists were considered and not done: the orchestrator cannot know before the run which tools a card needs, a short list stalls a paid run, and a long one adds nothing. This reason comes from the owner's request for the change; the commit message records the mechanism, not the motive.
How you notice it
kanban config set tools.smith '["Bash", "Read", "Edit", "Write"]' shortens smith's list for the next run. According to the comment at test_surface.py:107, --tools drops a name it does not know, so a misspelled tool name is likely to shorten the list without an error. A malformed value, such as a number in the list, is refused when you set it.

A hook replaces the per-type Agent grant +added−removed

What changed
The old agent files could say Agent(kanban-claude:card-helper), which lets a role start one subagent type. --tools cannot name an Agent(type), and its list also applies inside subagents, so a helper inherits the role's Agent tool. SPAWN_GUARD (runner.py:75) is a short Python program that settings_json (runner.py:143) puts into the run's --settings as a PreToolUse hook with matcher Agent|Task. It reads the hook input and exits 0 only when the requested subagent_type is the role's own helper (card-helper for smith, designer and scout, review-helper for warden) and the input has no agent_id. Claude Code sets agent_id only inside a subagent, so a helper cannot start anything. Every other case prints a message to stderr and exits 2, which blocks the call. So does any failure to read the event: invalid JSON, a null payload or a missing tool_input all run into a try/except that exits 2, because a PreToolUse hook that exits 1 is a non-blocking error and the tool would run. The program is a multi-line string, no longer a one-liner. A role with no helper (atlassian) gets an empty helper name, so every spawn is blocked.
Why
An allowlist of one: an agent type the deny list does not name, such as a user's own agent, stays out too. The deny list in role_denies (runner.py:134) is unchanged and still names the other helpers and the built-in agents, so the two layers overlap.
How you notice it
A smith that tries Explore, or a helper that tries to start another helper, has the call refused with the message kanban: only the role spawns, and only kanban-claude:card-helper. test_d1_a_role_may_spawn_only_its_own_helper_and_nothing_else (test_runner.py:189) runs the real command against each case, and test_d1_the_spawn_guard_blocks_when_it_cannot_read_the_event (test_runner.py:213) feeds it five unreadable payloads and expects exit 2 for each.

The write floor does not depend on the list =frozen~changed

What changed
NO_FILE_WRITES (runner.py:58) feeds role_denies, so warden and atlassian are denied Edit, Write and NotebookEdit, and scout is denied Edit and NotebookEdit, whatever tools.<role> holds. NotebookEdit is new in the set; before, it was blocked only because no agent file listed it.
Why
Once the agent file stops being the allowlist, a longer list in config could otherwise give a read-only role a file writer. The deny rules are the floor under the list, and a comment above the set says so.
How you notice it
kanban config set tools.warden '["Bash", "Read", "Edit"]' is accepted, and warden still cannot edit. test_surface.py:124 checks the denies instead of the tool list.

The atlassian role gets only its own server ~changed+added−removed

What changed
mcp_config (runner.py:162) no longer hands worker.mcp_allowlist to a role that owns a server: the atlassian role gets the atlassian server and nothing else, and the name atlassian is skipped when another role reads the allowlist. The server's entry gets ENABLED_TOOLS set to the 17 names in ATLASSIAN_TOOLS (runner.py:65): nine read tools and eight write tools. A comment says mcp-atlassian enforces the variable both when it lists and when it calls a tool. The agent file no longer lists the 17 mcp__atlassian__* names.
Why
The agent file used to hold both facts: which servers the role could see (by naming only atlassian tools) and which of that server's tools it could call. With tools: "*" neither survives in the file, so the runner now states both.
How you notice it
mcp_config(…, "atlassian", …) returns one server, whose env carries ENABLED_TOOLS. A setup that put atlassian in worker.mcp_allowlist to give it to every role no longer reaches the other roles. Because the agent files no longer filter MCP tools either, every other name in worker.mcp_allowlist is now available to all four builder and reviewer roles; the new test_only_the_designer_gets_the_browser asserts that playwright is not in the default allowlist for that reason.

Upgrade notes

Moving from dev8 to dev9

  1. Run the setup skill: /kanban-claude:setup. The diff changes no table, so there is no migration; the setup restarts the daemon on the new version.
  2. Runs already in flight keep the tool list they started with. The next run of each role uses the defaults in tools.<role>.
  3. New keys: tools.smith, tools.designer, tools.scout, tools.warden, tools.atlassian. Read one with kanban config get tools.smith and change it with kanban config set tools.smith '[…]'. To remove the helper from a role, leave Agent out of its list.
  4. If you put atlassian in worker.mcp_allowlist so other roles could reach it, remove it: only the atlassian role gets that server now.
  5. Any other name in worker.mcp_allowlist now reaches every dispatched role except atlassian, because no agent file narrows MCP tools any more.

Range covered

The diff runs from the tag v0.2.0.dev8 to 2a4aee8: 543b255 (a test fix for fake home paths), f9f01c0 (the feature), ec08adf (the version bump) and 2a4aee8 (the guard fix). The README, current_state.md and the CHANGELOG entry for 0.2.0.dev9 ship in the same range.

Quiz

Check what you took from this page

Five questions. Pick an answer to see the explanation.

1. Where does smith's list of built-in tools come from now?

build_argv adds --tools from tools.<role> (runner.py:305, :463). The agent file says tools: "*".

2. You set tools.warden to ["Bash", "Read", "Edit"]. Can warden edit files in its next run?

The deny rules sit under the list (NO_FILE_WRITES, runner.py:58). config_set only refuses items that are not strings.

3. Smith starts card-helper, and the helper tries to start card-helper in turn. What happens to the second spawn?

Claude Code sets agent_id in the hook input only inside a subagent, and the guard requires it to be absent (SPAWN_GUARD, runner.py:75).

4. Which MCP servers does the atlassian role start with?

mcp_config gives a role that owns a server nothing else, and adds ENABLED_TOOLS from ATLASSIAN_TOOLS (runner.py:162-182).

5. Which agent files still carry an explicit tool list?

The runner dispatches only the five roles; the helpers are started inside a run or by the orchestrator, so no config key covers them. test_surface.py:86 asserts "*" for the five and an explicit list for the rest.
